#!/bin/bash
# Add a private-prefix policy table without overwriting GRE/main-table routes.
# Losing the TUN cannot fall through to GRE or the public default.
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
config=${OP_WARP_SSH_CONFIG:-/etc/op-dbus/warp-ssh.json}
state=${OP_WARP_SSH_STATE_DIR:-/run/op-warp-ssh}
die() { printf 'warp-ssh routing: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
action=${1:-check}
case "$action" in activate|check|rollback) ;; *) die 'usage: routing.sh {activate|check|rollback}' ;; esac

command -v jq >/dev/null || die 'jq is required'
command -v flock >/dev/null || die 'flock is required'
mkdir -p "$state"
exec 9>"$state/routing.lock"
flock -n 9 || die 'another route operation is running'
manifest=$state/routing.json
if [ "$action" != activate ]; then
…
fi
jq -se 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "object")' "$config" >/dev/null || die 'expected one configuration object'
jq -e '
  def ipv4: type == "string" and
    (split(".") | length == 4 and all(.[];
      test("^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,2})$") and (tonumber <= 255)));
  def prefix: type == "string" and
    (split("/") | length == 2 and (.[0] | ipv4) and
      (.[1] | test("^([1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[0-2])$")));
  (.role == "host" or .role == "decoy") and
  (.tun_id | type == "number" and . == floor and . >= 0 and . <= 255) and
  ((.interface_name // ("tun" + (.tun_id | tostring))) | type == "string" and test("^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,15}$")) and
  (.mtu | type == "number" and . == floor and . >= 1280 and . <= 1500) and
  (.local_address | ipv4) and (.peer_address | ipv4) and
  .local_address != .peer_address and
  (.policy_table | type == "number" and . == floor and . >= 1000 and . <= 2147483647) and
  (.routes | type == "array" and length > 0 and length <= 64 and
    all(.[]; prefix) and (unique | length) == length) and
  (.rule_priority | type == "number" and . == floor and . > 0) and
  (.rule_priority + (.routes | length) < 32766)
' "$config" >/dev/null || die 'incomplete or invalid route configuration'
tun=$(jq -r '.interface_name // ("tun" + (.tun_id | tostring))' "$config")
peer=$(jq -r .peer_address "$config")
local_address=$(jq -r .local_address "$config")
table=$(jq -r .policy_table "$config")
first=$(jq -r .rule_priority "$config")
count=$(jq '.routes | length' "$config")
mtu=$(jq -r .mtu "$config")
prefixes=$(jq -r '.routes[]' "$config")

# These helpers inspect the live kernel only when an operator invokes this file.

routes_owned() { … }

check() { … }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Candidate preparation only. Never writes an existing file or starts Xray.
# INPUT_JSON PRIVATE_TRANSPORT_UUID_FILE DEDICATED_UDS_PATH NEW_PRIVATE_OUTPUT
set -euo pipefail
die() { printf 'central Xray proposal: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 4 ]] || die 'usage: INPUT_JSON PRIVATE_TRANSPORT_UUID_FILE DEDICATED_UDS_PATH NEW_PRIVATE_OUTPUT'
input=$1 credential=$2 socket=$3 output=$4
for file in "$input" "$credential"; do
    [[ -f $file && ! -L $file ]] || die 'input must be a regular non-symlink file'
done
[[ $(stat -c %u "$credential") == "$(id -u)" && $(stat -c %a "$credential") == 600 ]] || die 'transport UUID input must be owned by caller and mode 0600'
transport_uuid=$(cat -- "$credential")
[[ $transport_uuid =~ ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$ && $transport_uuid != 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 ]] || die 'invalid provided transport UUID'
[[ $socket == /* && $socket != *$'\n'* && $socket != *$'\r'* && $(realpath -m -- "$socket") == "$socket" && $socket != / ]] || die 'dedicated socket path must be absolute and canonical'
[[ ! -e $socket && ! -L $socket ]] || die 'dedicated socket pathname is already occupied'
[[ $output == /* && ! -e $output && ! -L $output && $(realpath -m -- "$output") == "$output" ]] || die 'output must be a new canonical absolute path'
parent=$(dirname -- "$output")
[[ -d $parent && ! -L $parent && $(realpath -e "$parent") == "$parent" && $(stat -c %u "$parent") == "$(id -u)" && $(stat -c %a "$parent") == 700 ]] || die 'output directory must be caller-owned mode 0700'
umask 077
stage=$(mktemp "$parent/.central-xray.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f -- "$stage"; unset transport_uuid' EXIT
# Pass the private UUID through stdin, not a command-line argument or log.
printf '%s' "$transport_uuid" | jq -R --slurp --slurpfile config "$input" --arg socket "$socket" '
    . as $id | $config[0] |
    "workspace-egress" as $tag |
    if ($config | length) != 1 or (.inbounds | type) != "array" or
       (.outbounds | type) != "array" or (.routing.rules | type) != "array" then
        error("unsupported canonical configuration shape")
    elif ([.outbounds[] | select(.tag == "od106-reality-egress" and .protocol == "vless")] | length) != 1 or
         ([.outbounds[] | select(.tag == "od106-reality-egress")] | length) != 1 then
        error("required unique existing REALITY VLESS outbound missing")
    elif any(.inbounds[]; .tag == $tag or .listen == $socket) or
         any(.routing.rules[]; (.inboundTag // [] | index($tag)) != null) then
        error("workspace tag or socket collision")
    elif any(.routing.rules[];
        .type != "field" or (.inboundTag | type) != "array" or (.inboundTag | length) == 0) then
        error("existing unscoped route could shadow appended workspace rule; operator review required")
    else
        .inbounds += [{tag:$tag,listen:$socket,protocol:"vless",
            settings:{clients:[{id:$id}],decryption:"none"},
            streamSettings:{network:"tcp",security:"none"}}] |
        .routing.rules += [{type:"field",inboundTag:[$tag],outboundTag:"od106-reality-egress"}]
    end
' > "$stage"
chmod 600 "$stage"
# An exclusive hard link publishes the complete candidate without overwriting
# an existing target, including one that appeared during preparation.
ln -- "$stage" "$output" || die 'candidate output collision'

#!/bin/bash
# The SSH carrier must never fall back to physical egress or into its TUN.
# Only this new connection is covered; the full WARP egress policy is separate.
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
config=${OP_WARP_SSH_CONFIG:-/etc/op-dbus/warp-ssh.json}
die() { printf 'warp-ssh guard: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v jq >/dev/null || die 'jq is required'
jq -se 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "object")' "$config" >/dev/null || die 'expected one configuration object'
jq -e '
  def ipv4: type == "string" and
    (split(".") | length == 4 and all(.[];
      test("^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,2})$") and (tonumber <= 255)));
  .role == "decoy" and (.ssh_host | ipv4) and
  (.ssh_port | type == "number" and . == floor and . > 0 and . <= 65535) and
  (.warp_interface | type == "string" and test("^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,15}$"))
' "$config" >/dev/null || die 'invalid decoy carrier configuration'
host=$(jq -r .ssh_host "$config")
port=$(jq -r .ssh_port "$config")
warp=$(jq -r .warp_interface "$config")
action=${1:-check}
case "$action" in install|check|remove) ;; *) die 'usage: guard.sh {install|check|remove}' ;; esac
state=${OP_WARP_SSH_STATE_DIR:-/run/op-warp-ssh}
mkdir -p "$state"
exec 8>"$state/guard.lock"
flock -n 8 || die 'another guard operation is running'

expected=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$expected"' EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' HUP TERM
cat > "$expected" <<EOF
table inet op_warp_ssh {
  comment "op-warp-ssh-owned"
  chain ssh_carrier {
    type filter hook output priority -10; policy accept;
    ip daddr $host tcp dport $port oifname != "$warp" counter drop comment "op-warp-ssh-carrier"
  }
}
EOF

check() {
    nft -j list table inet op_warp_ssh | jq -e \
      --arg host "$host" --argjson port "$port" --arg warp "$warp" '
      [.nftables[] | .table? // empty] as $t |
      [.nftables[] | .chain? // empty] as $c |
      [.nftables[] | .rule? // empty] as $r |
      ($t | length) == 1 and $t[0].comment == "op-warp-ssh-owned" and
      ($c | length) == 1 and $c[0].name == "ssh_carrier" and
      $c[0].type == "filter" and $c[0].hook == "output" and
      $c[0].prio == -10 and $c[0].policy == "accept" and
      ($r | length) == 1 and $r[0].chain == "ssh_carrier" and
      $r[0].comment == "op-warp-ssh-carrier" and
      ($r[0].expr | map(select(has("counter") | not))) == [
        {match:{op:"==",left:{payload:{protocol:"ip",field:"daddr"}},right:$host}},
        {match:{op:"==",left:{payload:{protocol:"tcp",field:"dport"}},right:$port}},
        {match:{op:"!=",left:{meta:{key:"oifname"}},right:$warp}},
        {drop:null}
      ]' >/dev/null
}
case "$action" in
    install)
        tables=$(nft -j list tables)
        if jq -e 'any(.nftables[].table?; .family == "inet" and .name == "op_warp_ssh")' <<<"$tables" >/dev/null; then
            check || die 'existing guard differs; refusing to overwrite it'
        else
            nft --check --file "$expected"
            nft --file "$expected"
            check || die 'guard readback differs'
        fi
        ;;
    check) check || die 'carrier guard is absent or differs' ;;
    remove)
        check || die 'guard differs; refusing to delete it'
        nft delete table inet op_warp_ssh
        ;;
esac

1:# VPS checklist — avoiding known incompatibilities
2:
3:Distilled from the 2026-08 flooding/mesh outage chain. Split by what you control
4:at **purchase time** (provider choice) and what must hold on **any host** you
5:run (design rules). Each item cites the incident that earned it.
6:
7:---
8:
9:## Part 1 — choosing a provider / box
10:
11:| check | why | incident |
12:|---|---|---|
13:| VRRP / proto 112 / multicast **not filtered** on customer ports | If filtered, the gateway MAC can never be learned → `actions=NORMAL` floods every gateway-bound frame to all ports. Forces static FDB pinning forever. | netcup filters VRRP; root of the flooding saga |
14:| KVM/dedicated with `/dev/net/tun`, cgroup2, nftables, loadable modules | OVS userspace datapath, WireGuard, and firewalling all need them. Containers/shared kernels break OVS in subtle ways. | — |
15:| UDP hairpin to own public IP works (`nc -u <own-ip> <own-port>`) | Some clouds (OCI) blackhole an instance talking to its own public endpoint. Self-referential WG peers then look "up" but carry 0 bytes. | decoy-wg2 self-peers, `10.0.0.1` unreachable |
16:| Public NIC MTU ≥ 1420 | Stack is tunnels-within-tunnels (WG inside WARP). Every missing byte costs MSS-clamp hacks per-path. | `mangle` clamp 1240 for netmaker 1280 |
17:| rDNS/PTR settable; IPv4 **and** IPv6 delegated | Mail legitimacy; REALITY `dest` credibility. | — |
18:
19:## Part 2 — design rules for any host we run
20:
21:1. **Never pin OpenFlow flows to an ofport.** The wire format carries port
22:   *numbers*; netclient recreates interfaces and numbers churn (88→199 on
23:   2026-08-24 overnight, mesh SSH died while handshakes stayed green).
24:   Re-bind by interface name at runtime; a watchdog must do this, not a human.
25:   Implemented: `/usr/local/libexec/3tched/ensure-ptap-flow.sh`, called from
26:   the `wg-3tched` loop.
27:2. **Nothing critical lives only in tmpfs without a boot-time restorer.**
28:   The sealed blob catalog lives in `/dev/shm`; when the stager regressed
29:   (`opblob stage-shm` missing from the installed binary), op-grpc-bridge
30:   crash-looped all boot and took the mesh 8090 door down with it.
31:3. **Every address has an owner service with a watchdog.** "netclient will
32:   assign it" is not ownership. `100.69.0.1` vanished mid-run once already;
33:   `wg-3tched` re-adds it every 10s and recreates the whole interface if the
34:   link disappears.
35:4. **One flow-table mutation path per flow class.** Controller-installed or
36:   watchdog-installed, never both drifting. Today's PTAP flow is explicitly a
37:   *stopgap* owned by the watchdog until `rovs-openflow` gains
38:   `packet_type` + `Encap` and the controller installs it itself.
39:5. **After any control-plane restart, verify the data plane.** WG handshakes
40:   prove only the outer tunnel. Inner packets can be black-holed at the bridge,
41:   firewall, or listener while every status looks green. The 60-second ritual:
42:   ```sh
43:   ovs-ofctl dump-flows -O OpenFlow15 ovsbr0 | grep packet_type  # counter moves?
44:   ip -s link show netmaker            # tx errors not climbing?

# VPS checklist — avoiding known incompatibilities

Distilled from the 2026-08 flooding/mesh outage chain. Split by what you control
at **purchase time** (provider choice) and what must hold on **any host** you
run (design rules). Each item cites the incident that earned it.

---

## Part 1 — choosing a provider / box

| check | why | incident |
|---|---|---|
| VRRP / proto 112 / multicast **not filtered** on customer ports | If filtered, the gateway MAC can never be learned → `actions=NORMAL` floods every gateway-bound frame to all ports. Forces static FDB pinning forever. | netcup filters VRRP; root of the flooding saga |
| KVM/dedicated with `/dev/net/tun`, cgroup2, nftables, loadable modules | OVS userspace datapath, WireGuard, and firewalling all need them. Containers/shared kernels break OVS in subtle ways. | — |
| UDP hairpin to own public IP works (`nc -u <own-ip> <own-port>`) | Some clouds (OCI) blackhole an instance talking to its own public endpoint. Self-referential WG peers then look "up" but carry 0 bytes. | decoy-wg2 self-peers, `10.0.0.1` unreachable |
| Public NIC MTU ≥ 1420 | Stack is tunnels-within-tunnels (WG inside WARP). Every missing byte costs MSS-clamp hacks per-path. | `mangle` clamp 1240 for netmaker 1280 |
| rDNS/PTR settable; IPv4 **and** IPv6 delegated | Mail legitimacy; REALITY `dest` credibility. | — |

## Part 2 — design rules for any host we run

1. **Never pin OpenFlow flows to an ofport.** The wire format carries port
   *numbers*; netclient recreates interfaces and numbers churn (88→199 on
   2026-08-24 overnight, mesh SSH died while handshakes stayed green).
   Re-bind by interface name at runtime; a watchdog must do this, not a human.
   Implemented: `/usr/local/libexec/3tched/ensure-ptap-flow.sh`, called from
   the `wg-3tched` loop.
2. **Nothing critical lives only in tmpfs without a boot-time restorer.**
   The sealed blob catalog lives in `/dev/shm`; when the stager regressed
   (`opblob stage-shm` missing from the installed binary), op-grpc-bridge
   crash-looped all boot and took the mesh 8090 door down with it.
3. **Every address has an owner service with a watchdog.** "netclient will
   assign it" is not ownership. `100.69.0.1` vanished mid-run once already;
   `wg-3tched` re-adds it every 10s and recreates the whole interface if the
   link disappears.
4. **One flow-table mutation path per flow class.** Controller-installed or
   watchdog-installed, never both drifting. Today's PTAP flow is explicitly a
   *stopgap* owned by the watchdog until `rovs-openflow` gains
   `packet_type` + `Encap` and the controller installs it itself.
5. **After any control-plane restart, verify the data plane.** WG handshakes
   prove only the outer tunnel. Inner packets can be black-holed at the bridge,
   firewall, or listener while every status looks green. The 60-second ritual:
   ```sh
   ovs-ofctl dump-flows -O OpenFlow15 ovsbr0 | grep packet_type  # counter moves?
   ip -s link show netmaker            # tx errors not climbing?
   ss -tln | grep '100.69.0.1:22'      # sshd still bound to the mesh IP?
   # from a peer:
   timeout 4 bash -c "</dev/tcp/100.69.0.1/22" && echo mesh-ssh-ok
   ```

## Known stacked firewalls on this host (check both after edits)

- `/etc/nftables.conf` — inet filter, policy drop, mesh allowlist by source subnet.
- `/etc/iptables/iptables.rules` — legacy iptables-nft table, restored at boot;
  its `ssh-public` DROP is scoped to `-i pub0`. A blanket port rule here silently
  shadows nft accepts because both tables hook input.

## Open items that keep biting

- ~~`opblob` binary lacks `stage-shm`/`persist`~~ FIXED 2026-08-25 (commit
  `22f44859`): subcommands restored from c4db14ae, binary rebuilt+deployed,
  persist→stage round trip verified. The hand-copy fallback in
  `opdbus-rundirs-up` remains as belt-and-suspenders.
- netclient v1.5 client vs v1.6 server (decoy) — MOOT for the mesh: netmaker
  broker retired 2026-08-25, both WG links are static confs now. Decoy's own
  egress is its self-contained wgcf-ingress (WARP), policy asserted by
  `mesh-policy.service`; its underlay to Cloudflare rides the VPS link
  (mark `0x7777` → table 51822 → MASQ out pub0).
- PTAP flow ownership: capability landed — vendored `rovs-openflow`
  (`vendor/rovs-openflow`, `[patch.crates-io]`) now encodes OXM_OF_PACKET_TYPE
  and OFPAT_ENCAP; translator installs via controller. RUNTIME BLOCKER left:
  OVS rejects the rovs-encoded FlowMod with error type=2 code=10 (BAD_ACTION)
  while identical semantics via `ovs-ofctl -O15 add-flow` install fine.
  Until that wire delta is root-caused (capture 6653 during a controller
  restart), the watchdog-owned flow stays authoritative: `ensure-ptap-flow.sh`
  + `ptap-watch`, and `openflow-static-flows.json` keeps the entry so the
  moment encoding matches, the controller takes over with no further change.
- Router (wrt-router) intentionally disconnected from this host: peer removed
  from static conf; its rc.local still dials a dead endpoint (harmless failed
  keepalives). Reconnect = re-add peer entry with pubkey
  `ppaYyM0y…`, or wipe its `/etc/rc.local` netmaker block.

content.text:
Yeah, you've got it split right — there are two different identity kinds here, and they don't mix:

- **GitHub = you.** That Copilot login is your personal GitHub identity doing chat. It's not bound to the server, and it's not a WireGuard peer.
- **Server/container = WireGuard keys.** Spark / Claude / other agent containers identify that way in this repo — identity sled (SID1) + WireGuard pubkey, provisioned container, session binding. A container is never the human; display alias is display-only.

So yes — keep the server's main identity on the WireGuard keys, not on the GitHub login.

On the hackathon part: I don't see any hackathon chatbot container defined in this tree — the only chatbot role in source is the control-plane chatbot, explicitly *not* a named assistant container. If you've got a separate hackathon container name/image somewhere, point me at it and I'll check how it's bound.

# Inbounds bind Unix sockets under /run/ghostbridge/xray; uds-xray-reality is the
# only TCP publication. The one live config path is /etc/xray/xray_config.json.
exec 2>&1
CONFIG=/etc/xray/xray_config.json
SOCK_DIR=/run/ghostbridge/xray

if [ ! -s "$CONFIG" ]; then
    echo "missing canonical Xray config $CONFIG"
    sleep 30
    exit 1
fi

install -d -o root -g root -m 0755 /run/ghostbridge
install -d -o xray -g xray -m 0750 "$SOCK_DIR"
rm -f "$SOCK_DIR"/*.sock "$SOCK_DIR"/*.sock.lock

export XRAY_LOCATION_ASSET=/usr/local/share/xray
if ! chpst -u xray:xray /usr/local/bin/xray run -test -config "$CONFIG" >/dev/null; then
